newsitem.title: JAPAN: Long-awaited Japan-Russia PGM contract talks start.
newsitem.headline: Long-awaited Japan-Russia PGM contract talks start.

text.p: Long-awaited talks between Japan and Russia on platinum group metal (PGM) exports for 1997 started on Monday after Russian officials arrived in Tokyo over the weekend, Japanese precious metal traders said.
Russian PGM shipments are expected to resume as early as late June if the contract talks progress smoothly, they said.
Russian officials Vitaly Berlin and Andrei Travkin from Russia's PGM export agency Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) are now in Tokyo to talk with Japanese clients on PGM contracts.
"The agency started talks on PGMs with Japanese trade houses today," an official with a bullion house said.
Another trader in Tokyo said he believed shipments could resume in July, with prices based on average palladium prices in June.
The Russian export agency officials were not immediately available for comment.
Russia has not exported any PGMs so far in 1997, with officials in Moscow citing bureaucratic problems and delays in passing the federal budget as the main reasons for the hold-up.
Yen-based palladium futures on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange ended sharply lower on Monday amid expectations that Russia will resume PGM exports soon.
Benchmark April palladium ended 21 yen weaker at 584 yen per gram, after plunging its 24-yen daily limit at the opening.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of PGMs. Russia is the world's top supplier of palladium and the second-largest supplier of platinum.
Palladium prices have surged in recent months on the absence of Russian exports.
